label: accepted

evidence.V1: Reads as a coursed stone wall section from front and three-quarter; silhouette and top are a clean slab as a modular piece should be.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: wall slab, medium cap/plinth/courses, small chamfers and recessed joints.
evidence.V3: Stones are near-square uniform tiles with thin sliver stones at the left edge; tidy but stiff rather than confidently stylised.
evidence.V4: Consistent small chamfers on every stone, cap and plinth that catch the light in the face and top close-ups.
evidence.V5: Face, top and end-section close-ups are clean: no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in ~3 grey values with a darker plinth; brick and sandstone colourways keep the value structure.
evidence.V7: 572 tris vs module target 800 - under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, chamfered made-object edges, stone hue in 3 values; matches the modular kit spec.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, Color white, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes (iou 0.98, cover 1.0).

evidence.V1: Front and 3/4 read as a stone wall through the course pattern, but the silhouette is a plain rectangular slab - only the shaded views identify it.
evidence.V2: Big slab, medium courses + darker plinth + cap; nothing at the small scale beyond chamfers, so hierarchy is only partial.
evidence.V3: Chunky chamfered stones suit the style but they are near-square blocks in a regular grid with little size variation; reads stiff.
evidence.V4: All stones, plinth and cap share a consistent chamfer that catches the light in face/top/end close-ups.
evidence.V5: Studio close-ups clean; face_flat shows only a 1-2 px dark speck at a block corner, otherwise no seams, pinches or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Single stone hue in three values (light/mid/dark plinth); colourways keep the value structure.
evidence.V8: White vertex-colour material, chamfered stone blocks, stone hue only - matches modular kit spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling pass (iou 0.98).

evidence.V1: Reads as a stone wall section from front, three-quarter and silhouette (slab with coursed block notches along the edge); top view is a clean bar, as expected for a straight module.
evidence.V2: Big slab, cap ledge and plinth course plus medium block coursing, but no small tier (no chipped blocks, through-stones or mortar accents).
evidence.V3: Staggered coursing and value-varied blocks help, but blocks are near-uniform rectangles with a thin cap; partly stylised, still stiff.
evidence.V4: Every block, the plinth and the cap ledge carry the same small chamfer that catches light in the face, top and end close-ups.
evidence.V5: Face, top and end-section close-ups (studio and flat) show clean flat shading; no pinches, seams or z-fighting; 0 cross-shell overlaps.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in about 3 values with a darker plinth; slate and sandstone colourways keep the value structure.
evidence.V7: 572 tris vs module target 800, under target.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, stone hue values and kit-scale chamfers; matches the modular kit (end faces are plain but hidden when tiled).
evidence.V9: Studio line correct (anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, white colour, grid-corner pivot); T1 tiling pass on the 2-stud grid.

artifacts: Possible 1-2 px pinhole/speck at a block corner in face_flat close-up
top_fixes: Vary stone widths more and avoid thin sliver stones at the panel edge
Add slight per-stone inset/bulge or edge irregularity for stylised character
Consider wrapping stone joints onto the plain end face
Vary stone widths/heights more (running bond with long and short stones) to break the square grid
Add a small-scale tier (a few chipped/proud stones, or a subtle gold/iron accent) for hierarchy
Check the tiny speck at the block corner for a micro gap between shells
Add a small tier: a few chipped/bevelled-out blocks, a through-stone or slight block protrusion variation
Vary block sizes and give the cap ledge a little more depth/overhang for a more confident stylised read
Dress the exposed end with block returns for wall-run terminations
